title: Control hover detection behaves unexpectedly with Viewports
body:
### Tested versions

I've tested only on Godot v4.7.2.stable

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1074) - AMD Ryzen 9 5950X 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 63.94 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Surround 7.1)

### Issue description

I’m trying to horizontally flip an entire viewport/container using a shader.

To make mouse interaction match the flipped rendering, I also added a script to the container that intercepts mouse events and horizontally flips their coordinates before forwarding them with `push_input`.

The mouse click works correctly with the transformed coordinates, but hover does not.



### Steps to reproduce

1. Apply a horizontal flip to the entire scene using a shader on the container.
2. Intercept mouse events on the same container.
3. Horizontally flip the mouse coordinates.
4. Forward the modified events using `push_input`.
5. Observe that clicks work correctly, but hover detection remains at the original Control position.

Flipping shader (as the material for the vp container):
```glsl
shader_type canvas_item;

void fragment() {
    vec2 uv = UV;
    uv.x = 1.0 - uv.x;

    COLOR = texture(TEXTURE, uv);
}
```

Flipping sciprt (for flipping coordinates)
```gdscript
extends SubViewportContainer

@onready var _VIEWPORT: SubViewport = $SubViewport

func _ready() -> void:
	_VIEWPORT.handle_input_locally = false

func _propagate_input_event(_event: InputEvent) -> bool:
	return false

# Since the viewport is flipped via the shader i'm flipping all mouse events (horizontally)
func _gui_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
	if !(event is InputEventMouse): return
	
	var event_new : InputEventMouse = event.duplicate()
	event_new.position.x = _VIEWPORT.size.x - event_new.position.x
	event_new.global_position.x = _VIEWPORT.size.x - event_new.global_position.x
	
	if event_new is InputEventMouseMotion:
		event_new.relative.x = _VIEWPORT.size.x - event_new.relative.x
		
	_VIEWPORT.push_input(event_new, true)
```
